q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a bank branch?
title: Bank branch carbon footprint
short: Add each branch's electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, generator diesel at 2.68 kg per litre and AC refrigerant top-ups. Sum branches for the operational footprint. Loans and investments are a separate figure, financed emissions in Scope 3 Category 15, not part of the branch number.
audience: Banks, NBFCs and cooperative banks with branch networks

ul: Electricity from the branch bill, including ATMs on the same meter.
Refrigerant top-ups from AC service invoices.

p: Most branches are rented. If the bank runs the space and pays the bill, the electricity is Scope 2 under operational control.
Emissions of borrowers and investee companies go in Category 15 under the PCAF method. Report them separately from the branch footprint.

example.title: Worked example: one branch (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Branch total: 2,887 kg CO2 a month, 34.6 t a year
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; repeat for each branch from its own bills.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
